title: Pool of Radiance
build: version 1.0, eight D64 images (archive.org d64_Pool_of_Radiance_v1.0_1988_SSI_Disk_1_of_4_Side_A); BOOT prints "POOL OF RADIANCE, VERSION 1.0"

records.c: The camp module's start, which the linker calls with JSR $0800 at $2BB5: sets the member on view from the party cursor (pick_view_member) and falls into camp_restart.

The rest of the start, also the module's second entry, which LIBRARY's jump table passes on from $2C90. A minute passes (pass_minutes). When the adventure's CAST sent the party here ($6DAB set), it goes straight to cast_command and leaves. Otherwise it draws the camp screen, lets items marked NOT HERE be readied ($6DE4 = 1), prints YOU SET UP CAMP..., starts the rest's counters (the interruption check every $6DD2 passes, an hour of 12 passes, a day of 24 hours), cancels any half-finished studies (cancel_studies) and puts the camp's own item actions in LIBRARY's tables (set_camp_actions).

The ENCAMP menu: SAVE VIEW MAGIC REST ALTER EXIT on the bottom row, with the cursor where it was last ($286B); up and down move the party cursor meanwhile ($2861 = $FF, run_menu). EXIT leaves, and the left arrow only shows the menu again; a choice is called through the self-modified JSR at $0883 from encamp_handlers, and the menu comes back unless the rest was interrupted ($6DD3 negative).

Leaves the camp: the next module is DUNGEON ($6E11 = 1), the CAST and NOT HERE flags are cleared, the studies cancelled, LIBRARY's own item actions put back (set_item_actions with X = $16) and the area's script ($49F2) loaded into slot 8 again, since the camp loads the spell table there; load_resource_a returns to the linker.
A choice: its routine's address from encamp_handlers goes into the JSR at $0883.
The operand of the ENCAMP menu's JSR at $0883: the chosen command's routine, low byte.
The ENCAMP menu's call, high byte.
After a command: a rest that was interrupted ($6DD3 = $FF) leaves the camp at once, so that the adventure module can run the encounter.
The ENCAMP commands' routines in menu order: SAVE save_command, VIEW view_command, MAGIC magic_command, REST rest_command, ALTER alter_command.
encamp_handlers read for the high bytes: the ENCAMP menu's LDA at $087D takes each routine's high byte from here.
The ENCAMP menu for menu_bar: the count (6), the heading ENCAMP:, then SAVE, VIEW, MAGIC, REST, ALTER and EXIT.
The ALTER menu: the count (6), ALTER:, then ORDER, DROP, SPEED, ICON, PICS and EXIT.

ALTER: its menu, with the cursor where it was last ($286C) and the party cursor live; a choice runs through the JSR at $0916 from alter_handlers, and EXIT or the left arrow returns to the ENCAMP menu.
The operand of ALTER's JSR at $0916, low byte.
ALTER's call, high byte.
ALTER's routines: ORDER order_command, DROP drop_command, SPEED speed_command, ICON icon_command, PICS pics_command.
alter_handlers read for the high bytes, by ALTER's LDA at $0910.

ICON: changes the combat icon of the member on view. Keeps the disk side in the drive, asks for side 3 (want_disk_side), loads SPELLN64, the icon editor, into slot 6 ($AF00), copies the member's 36-byte icon (point_at_icon) to the editor's working copy at $AF00 and calls icon_editor ($AF24). Then, on a dark grey background, ARE YOU SURE ABOUT YOUR NEW COMBAT ICON? (message 41): OKAY copies the edited icon back over the member's. Puts the black background back, asks for the old side again and redraws the camp screen.
The PICS menu: the count (5), PICS:, then CHARACTERS OFF, CHARACTERS ON, MONSTERS OFF, MONSTERS ON and EXIT; the item names the switch as it stands, and pics_command shows one of each pair.

PICS: the picture switches in $49FF. Shows CHARACTERS ON when the portraits are on (bit 7) and CHARACTERS OFF when not, the same for MONSTERS by bit 0, then EXIT. Choosing an item turns its switch the other way (pics_keep_masks and pics_set_bits) and shows the menu again, cursor on MONSTERS; EXIT returns.
For each PICS item, the bits of $49FF it keeps: $81, $01, $81, $80 (CHARACTERS OFF and ON, MONSTERS OFF and ON). The other bits are cleared on the way.
For each PICS item, the bit it then sets: $80 turns the portraits on, $01 the monsters' pictures; the ON items set nothing, so their bit stays cleared.

ORDER: puts the party in a new order. Every member starts unplaced ($28CE = $FF) and the party list shows them (order_list). For each position from 1 to the number in the party it asks WHO TAKES POSITION #n? (message 24, the digit at $24F4) over the party list (choose_member): a member not yet placed takes the position, with one of TAKES THE POSITION, LEAPS INTO PLACE or STANDS READY at random (messages 49-51), and the numbers beside the names are redrawn (order_numbers). EXIT takes back the last position given; taking back past the first leaves with nothing changed.
The member chosen: one placed already is asked for again.

All placed: slots 7 and 8 ($6E1A, $6E1B) are marked to load again, because the copies about to be made run from $9900 over the spell routines and the script. Then each of the eight slots in turn is copied out, $244 bytes after the last: its character, its party entry and its second page ($220 bytes from $6B00, through copy_ram) and its combat icon (36 bytes), from $9900 on.
The eight party entries and their characters are cleared and stored empty.

Then, from slot 7 down, each member goes to its new place P ($28CE): the timed effects on its old slot are moved onto P ($4940), its $220 bytes are copied back to $6B00 with its slot ($6C0D) set to P and stored there, and its icon goes to $4BE0 + 36 times P. The effects are moved one slot at a time over the same column, so an effect moved onto a slot that is handled later is moved a second time.
The party list in the right-hand panel (party_list_panel), then order_numbers.

Beside each member placed so far, in cyan at column 12, its new position in brackets (message 48, "( )", with the digit at $2696), one row each from row 4 in the list's order. The colour goes back to green ($6E34 = 5).

DROP: removes the member on view from the party, unless it is the only one. Shows its name with WILL BE GONE FOREVER (message 60) and asks ARE YOU SURE ABOUT DROPPING THIS CHARACTER? (message 61). OKAY: the name with BIDS YOU FAREWELL (message 63), or IS DUMPED IN A DITCH (64) when it is down (bit 7 of $6C00); its name and party entry are cleared and stored, its timed effects ended (their kind set to 0), and the party cursor goes to the top. CANCEL: a member who is down is passed over in silence, the others get BREATHES A SIGH OF RELIEF (message 69).
CANCEL.
The SPEED menu: the count (3), SPEED:, then SLOWER, FASTER and EXIT.

SPEED: shows GAMESPEED = (0=FAST 9=SLOW) (message 7) with the message speed ($49FC) printed in it at column 12, and the menu SLOWER FASTER EXIT: SLOWER adds one to it, up to 9, and FASTER takes one away, down to 0; at either end the item that would go past is left out of the menu.

SAVE: keeps the disk side ($2863, and $49EA in the saved game), prints INSERT YOUR SAVE GAME DISK (message 23) with PRESS ANY KEY TO CONTINUE (37) and waits, then forgets the side ($6E12 = $FF) and offers SAVE GAME or EXIT (save_menu_text).
The operand of LDA $6E12; DUNGEON2's code at $7AAC refers to $0CAD, which is the adventure module's message table when that module is in.

SAVE GAME: prints SAVING (message 27), cancels any half-finished studies (cancel_studies), so that a saved game holds no spells half memorized, and marks slots 9, 18, 19 and 20 (save_reload_slots) to load again. Puts the KERNAL's own vectors back (RESTOR, $FF8A), so that saving goes through the KERNAL rather than the fast loader, resets the drive with "UI" (reset_drive) and reads its error channel. The files in the 25 resource slots ($6E13-$6E2B) are kept at $4BC0, slot 8's as the area's own script ($49F2) rather than the spell table the camp may have in it.

Saves file $28DD, SAVEDGAME1 first and then SAVEDGAME0 (the digit at $0DCC): file 1 from $8300 to $8AFF, the party's entries, and file 0 from $4900 to $64FF, the saved game and the characters (save_start_lo to save_end_hi). An error 63 from save_file, the drive's FILE EXISTS, scratches the old file (scratch_save_file) and saves again; any other error, or a bad status after the save (save_status), prints --SAVE ERROR-- (message 25) and offers TRY AGAIN: YES NO, where NO gives up.

The end of SAVE, saved or not: asks for the game disk's side again (want_disk_side), and when the player kept the fast loader ($6DE5 = 0) loads its drive half, PIC64, into slot 5 and installs it again (install_fast_loader, $6D9F = 1). Then the camp picture is drawn again.
SAVE's menu: the count (2), no heading, SAVE GAME and EXIT; at $0DA4 the second, the count (2), TRY AGAIN:, YES and NO.
The menu after a failed save: TRY AGAIN: YES NO.
The two save files' start addresses, low bytes (file 0 at $0DB8, file 1 at $0DB9): $00 and $00.
Their high bytes: $49 for file 0 ($4900) and $83 for file 1 ($8300).
The addresses the saves stop before, low bytes: $00 and $00.
Their high bytes: $65 ($6500) for file 0 and $8B ($8B00) for file 1.
"S0:SAVEDGAME" and the digit at $0DCC: the drive's scratch command for a save file, 13 characters (scratch_save_file); the file name itself starts at $0DC3.
The save file's name, SAVEDGAME and the digit at $0DCC: ten characters.
The save file's digit, written as "0" plus the file number ($28DD) before each save.
"UI", the drive command that resets the drive (reset_drive), which clears the fast loader's code from the drive before the KERNAL saves.
The resource slots SAVE marks to load again: 9 (WALLS) and 18 to 20 (the three WALLDEFs).
Sends "S0:SAVEDGAMEn" on the command channel (disk_command), deleting the save file so that it can be saved again.
Sends "UI" on the command channel (disk_command) and waits a moment (delay with A = 0).
After a save: initialises the drive again (drive_init) and returns its status, 0 when the save went through.

Copies with all 64 KB of RAM switched in (all_ram): X bytes, then Y more pages of 256, from the address in the LDA at $0E03 to the one in the STA at $0E06, both counting on as it goes, so that copies made one after another follow each other. Switches the ROMs and I/O back in at the end ($3AB1).
The operand of copy_ram's LDA at $0E03: where it copies from, low byte; set by the caller and counted on as it goes.
copy_ram's source, high byte.
The operand of copy_ram's STA at $0E06: where it copies to, low byte.
copy_ram's destination, high byte.
The source address's high byte goes up when its low byte comes round to 0.
Prints camp message X at the start of the next row of the text window.
Prints camp message X at the cursor.
Prints camp message X at row A, column Y: its address from camp_message_lo and camp_message_hi into the string pointer ($07/$08), then print_string.
print_string for the string at A (low) and Y (high).
Prints the character A at the cursor: stores it as message 34, a single character and a zero, and prints that.
The cursor's column to A columns in from the window's left edge.

The camp screen's five frames, four bytes each: left column, top row, right column and bottom row. 0 the picture's frame (0,0 to 16,16), 1 the lower text area (0,16 to 39,23), 2 the right-hand panel (16,0 to 39,16), 3 the whole screen (0,0 to 39,23), 4 the picture itself (2,2 to 14,14).
Window 1's four bytes, the lower text area: the address the LDA at $0E92 holds in the file, before set_window first writes it.
camp_window's order of the frame's bytes for the window's left, right, top and bottom edges ($03F2-$03F5): 0, 2, 1, 3.
What camp_window adds to each: one to the left and top edges, nothing to the right and bottom, so that the text sits inside the frame's lines.
camp_window for window X, then draws its frame with corner squares (draw_box_corners), from the four bytes the LDA at $0E92 was pointed at.

Sets the text window ($03F2-$03F5) inside frame X of window_edges and puts the cursor at its top left. The frame's address, $0E54 plus four times X, is written into the LDA at $0E92 itself (window_ptr_lo and window_ptr_hi).
The operand of camp_window's LDA at $0E92: the chosen frame's four bytes, low byte; framed_window passes it on to draw_box_corners.
The frame's address, high byte.
run_menu with the cursor on the first item and every item offered.
run_menu with every item offered (the mask A = $FF), the cursor at $286A.

Prints the menu bar X/Y (menu_bar's $3D55, with the items in mask A) and waits for a choice, the cursor at $286A. While nothing is pressed it counts about 76 times 256 polls, then animates the camp picture on every poll while $2880 is set. Up and down move the party cursor when $2861 is set (party_cursor), and the member on view with it. Returns the item chosen in A, $FF for the left arrow, and the cursor in X ($286A), with $2861 cleared.
A key or the joystick: the idle count starts again; menu_key makes a choice of it.
A choice.
The member on view ($6EFC) is the party slot on the cursor's row of the party list ($6E36 + $6D7B).
Prints, typed out, the working member's name at the next row, then message X after it, then spell Y's name on the row below (print_spell_line), and pauses: "NAME CASTS" and the spell, for instance.
Spell Y's name at the start of the next row.
Prints spell Y's name from SPELLN00's tables at $AF00 (low bytes) and $AF80 (high bytes).
In the lower window: the working member's name, message X after it typed out, a pause, then the window cleared.
Clears the lower window and types message X in it.
Types message $2864 at the next row of the window.
Keeps X as the message number ($2864), sets the text window to the lower area and clears it.
Sets the lower text area with its frame and clears it.
Waits by the message speed ($49FC), then stops the typing.
No text delay ($03FC = 0): text prints at once.
The text delay to four times the message speed, so that text appears typed.
Types message X on the bottom row, from column 0, after blanking it.
Loads the member on view ($6EFC) and its character.
Loads party slot A ($6DB4) and its character.
Loads party slot $6DB4 and its character, returning 0; a negative slot loads nothing and returns it.

Asks for disk side A unless the drive has it already ($6E12): INSERT YOUR GAME DISK #n (message 70, the digit at $27BB) and PRESS ANY KEY TO CONTINUE, then waits for a key and takes A as the side in the drive.

Draws the picture's frame and clears it, then the picture's own frame (window 4, $2880 = 4); unless the party came for CAST, loads ANIMATE00 (slot 11) and PIC1D, the camp's picture (slot 5), and starts it (start_view_picture, animate_frame).
Points $9E/$9F at the combat icon of character slot $6DB1, $4BE0 plus 36 times the slot.
set_item_actions with X = $0A: the camp's own six.

Copies six routines (X = $0A the camp's, $16 LIBRARY's own) from camp_item_actions into LIBRARY's item actions READY, USE, TRADE, DROP, HALVE and JOIN ($4611/$4619). Whichever, it also points the VIEW screen's TRADE at trade_money ($4471), its DROP at drop_money ($447B) and its SPELLS at view_spells ($4481), LIBRARY's frame call at draw_box_corners ($48C8), and offers every VIEW choice ($6EF7 = $FF).
The camp's item actions: READY camp_ready, USE camp_use, TRADE camp_trade, DROP camp_drop, HALVE camp_halve, JOIN camp_join.
The item action tables read for the high bytes, by set_item_actions's LDA at $1049.
LIBRARY's own, put back on leaving: READY $4630, none for USE, TRADE $4743, DROP $47DA, none for HALVE or JOIN ($FFFF).

VIEW: the VIEW screen for the member on view (view_menu), offering every item action ($6EF8 = $3F) to a member who can act, and all but USE ($3D) to one who is down or dead; items show as magical when a timed effect of kind 5 is on (check_detect). Then the camp screen again.
READY: readies or puts away the item in hand (ready_item), then item_effect.

An item with bit 7 of $6D8B set has an effect while it is readied, of that kind ($6E6E): its handler is called (call_effect_handler) with $28E7 = 0 when the item is now readied and $80 when it is not. Then the item is stored and the member's figures worked out again.
The member's combat figures again (compute_combat_stats), the member stored, and the screen's frame redrawn.

DROP: a scroll being scribed from asks first (check_scribing, DROPPING THAT ITEM?); otherwise the item's name with WILL BE GONE FOREVER (message 60) and ARE YOU SURE ABOUT DROPPING THAT ITEM? (43). OKAY empties the slot ($6D7C and $6D82 to 0), so that the effect of a readied item ends with it (item_effect).
TRADE: a scroll being scribed from asks first (TRADING IT?, message 44); then LIBRARY's trade_item gives the item to the member chosen.

USE: casts a spell from the item in hand, which must be readied (MUST BE READIED, message 4, otherwise). A scroll (is_scroll) asks first if it is being scribed from (CASTING A SPELL FROM IT?, message 45), then lists its spells (list_scroll) for one to be picked under CAST and 'S SCROLL; it is cast at level 6 from the scroll ($28E4 = 1). Another item casts the spell in $6D8A, less $17 from $50 up, unless it has none or bit 7 of $6D8B is set ($28E4 = 2).
The cast: caster level ($2878) 6, the user as caster, cast_spell.
When the spell was cast ($28E3): the item is loaded again; a scroll loses the spell (use_scroll_word), another item a charge (use_charge).
The scroll's spell is cleared from its three ($6D89-$6D8B).
One charge less ($6D89); with the last, one of the stack goes ($6D86), or, with only one, the item itself.
The item and the character stored.
Carry set for an item of type $0B to $0D ($6D8C), the scrolls.

For DROP, TRADE and USE, X the question: when the item is a type $0B scroll and the member is scribing from it (an entry of the member's in the scribe list, scribe_list, whose low four bits are the item's slot), shows the name with IS SCRIBING FROM THAT SCROLL (message 42) and asks ARE YOU SURE ABOUT and question X. OKAY crosses that entry out ($FF) and returns carry clear, CANCEL carry set; with no such entry it returns a negative A.
The branch's offset; the stray reference to $120F comes from bytes at $AF27, whatever is loaded there.

Adds one to clock figure X ($49C6 + X) and carries on into the next while a figure comes round to 0 (clock_limits); each figure that comes round sets its bit in $28E6. When the days figure comes round (once a month) the days gone by ($49EC/$49ED) go up by one: the adventure module counts every day there, the camp only the months. Past the months the year goes up ($49CC/$49CD).
Each clock figure's limit: 10, 10 minutes, 6 tens of minutes, 24 hours, 30 days, 12 months.

Passes A minutes: adds them one at a time to the minutes figure (clock_add), then, unless $28C6 is set, ages every timed effect with time left (age_effect) and ends the ones that run out (end_effect).

The time left A of a timed effect, aged: one counted in minutes (top bits 0) loses the minutes passed ($2865), down to 0; one counted in ten-minute turns, hours or days (top bits 1 to 3) loses one when that unit's figure came round ($28E6, by bit_of), keeping its unit, and reaches 0 when its count was 1. Returns the new byte.
Code nothing calls: for the member $6DB4 having item type A (has_item_type), the effect's handler would be called with $28E7 = 0 (call_effect_handler).

Loads the spell files (load_spell_files), finds the effect kind $6E6E in ECL65's list at $9AD5 (zero-terminated) and calls its handler, from $9AEE (low bytes) and $9B06 (high bytes), through the self-modified JSR at $1319 with A = $28E7; then stores the member. A kind not in the list calls nothing.
The operand of the JSR at $1319: the effect handler, low byte.
The effect handler, high byte.

Ends timed effect X: its kind goes to $6E6E and the entry is emptied. When the value it kept at $4B80 has bit 7 set, the member it was on ($4940) is loaded and the kind's handler called with that value (call_effect_handler).
Loads SPELLE04, the spell routines, into slot 7 ($A700), then falls into load_spell_table and load_spell_names.
Loads ECL65, the spell table and the effect handlers, into slot 8 ($9900), then load_spell_names.
Loads SPELLN00, the spells' names, into slot 6 ($AF00).
add_exit_item_at at the window's left edge.

Adds EXIT (message 10) to the menu on show, at row Y and A columns in: its column, row, width 4 and key $FF go in the menu's tables ($6EAA, $6EBE, $6ED2, $6E96), the menu is a vertical one ($6E94 = 0), and EXIT is printed there.
The party list in the right-hand panel with the chosen member in white ($6DE0 = 1).
Clears the right-hand panel and lists the party in it ($3E06).
Draws the whole camp screen: the outer frame, the party list, the lower window and the picture, and blanks the menu bar.
The lower window's frame, the picture (draw_camp_picture) and a blank menu bar.
The whole screen's frame with its corners, the picture stopped ($2880 = 0) and the window cleared.

Draws the frame at A/X (draw_box), then puts the font's corner square (character 0) in yellow at its four corners, and the text colour back ($6E34). LIBRARY's frame call ($48C7) is pointed here while the camp runs, so that the VIEW screen's frames get corners too.
The corner squares on row A, at the frame's left and right columns ($48F2, $48F4).
member_can_act_msg for the member on view.
member_can_act for slot A; one that cannot gets the name and CAN'T DO THAT (message 30). Carry set when it cannot.
Loads party slot A; carry set when it is down (bit 7 of $6C00) or DEAD (condition 3).

Casts spell $29BF ($28E3 = 0 until it is cast): takes its seven bytes from the spell table (get_spell_data). A spell with no target outside combat ($28C9 = 0) goes to combat_only_spell, unless it comes from an item ($28E4 = 2). Otherwise the spell files are loaded, SPELLE04's choose_target ($A700) gives the target, carry clear for none, which is kept in $28DE; the cast is announced and the spell taken from memory (announce_cast), and its handler ($28CC/$28CD) is jumped to.
Loads the spell table (load_spell_table) and copies spell $29BF's seven bytes, from $9900 plus seven times one less, to spell_data ($28C7-$28CD).

Marks the spell cast ($28E3) and stores the character; a memorized spell ($28E4 = 0) is first found among the memorized ($6B20-$6B70, from the last) and cleared, and when it is not there nothing is marked.

The spell's name with IS A COMBAT ONLY SPELL (message 33), and ARE YOU SURE ABOUT CASTING THIS SPELL? (71). OKAY marks it cast and, from memory, forgets it (forget_spell): the spell is lost and has no effect.
Loads the caster ($2870) again; unless the spell comes from an item ($28E4 = 2), prints the caster's name, CASTS (message 29) and the spell's name ($6DCE). Then forget_spell.
The MAGIC menu: the count (6), no heading, then CAST, MEMORIZE, SCRIBE, DISPLAY, REST and EXIT.

MAGIC: its menu, the cursor where it was last ($286D) and the party cursor live; CAST is left out while $49E5 is set. The spells' names are loaded (load_spell_names) and a choice called through the JSR at $1519 from magic_handlers; the menu comes back until EXIT, or until the rest was interrupted ($6DD3 = $FF).
The operand of MAGIC's JSR at $1519, low byte.
MAGIC's call, high byte.
MAGIC's routines: CAST cast_command, MEMORIZE memorize_command, SCRIBE scribe_command, DISPLAY display_command, REST rest_command.
magic_handlers read for the high bytes, by MAGIC's LDA at $1510.

SCRIBE, for the member on view: spells it has chosen to scribe already are shown for confirming (confirm_scribing), and OKAY keeps them. Otherwise the list is cleared and the scrolls it can copy from listed (list_scroll_spells): none gives HAS NO COPYABLE SCROLLS (message 46). The spells are picked under SCRIBE and 'S SCROLL (spell_screen), then confirmed, and CANCEL clears them all.
list_scribing, then confirm_chosen.

The member's entries in the scribe list (from $6C01, $6C02 of them), the spells only, into the spell list at $9700 ($29BD of them); the party entry is loaded again afterwards, since the count was used up.

The spell picked, $2891 on the page that starts at $29B9: its entry ($28E8: which of the scroll's spells and the item's slot) is checked (check_scribe); a good one is added to the scribe list (scribe_list, at $2894) and to the member's count ($6C02), its level adds to the member's levels to scribe ($289B), and the hours of rest before studying ($28B3) go up to the level's (rest_hours_by_level). Prints WILL SCRIBE (message 21), or the reason not, with the spell's name, and the page again.

Carry clear when the spell may be scribed; otherwise carry set and X the message: --NO MORE SCRIBING-- (20) with the scribe list full ($2894 negative), IS ALREADY SCRIBING (19) when it is among the member's entries already, ALREADY KNOWS (18) when its bit is set in the spell book ($6B78), CAN'T SCRIBE (17) when the member has no spells of its level for its class ($6BED + level, the low four bits for a magic-user's spell, the high four for a cleric's). A member with no entries yet starts its list at the list's end ($6C01).
The eight bits, 1 to $80, by their number.

SCRIBE's list: for each item carried, from slot 15 down, a scroll (is_scroll) whose classes ($6D99) share one with the member's ($6BEB) has its spells listed (list_scroll), and each goes on the list with, in $28E8, which of the three it is (times 16) and the item's slot. The list is built at $9703 and moved down to $9700; $29BD the count.

DISPLAY: DISPLAY SPELLS ON WHOM? over the party list with THE WHOLE PARTY (message 31, in cyan) as an extra row; EXIT leaves. For the member, or for effects on the whole party ($FF), each effect kind from 1 to 63 that is on it (find_entry_x, or find_entry for each member) is named by the spell whose kind byte ($28CA, without bit 7) is that kind, eighteen to a page, with PRESS ANY KEY TO CONTINUE between pages and at the end.
DISPLAY's page: the member's name or THE WHOLE PARTY, then IS AFFECTED BY: (message 53); eighteen rows to fill ($287D).

CAST, from the MAGIC menu or from the adventure's CAST: the member on view casts. One who cannot act gets CAN'T DO THAT. The spells being memorized (bit 7 of $6B20 and on) are set aside in $28E8 for the while, so that only those memorized can be cast; none gives HAS NO SPELLS MEMORIZED (message 38). The spells memorized are listed (list_memorized) under CAST and 'S MEMORIZED (spell_screen). Afterwards the spells set aside are put back, and the camp screen is drawn again if there were any to cast.
Casts the spell picked ($29BF) for the member $2870, at its class's level: $6BCA, the cleric level, for a cleric's spell (bit 7 of $28CA) and $6BC9, the magic-user level, otherwise (cast_spell).

MEMORIZE, for the member on view: spells chosen to memorize already are shown for confirming (confirm_memorizing), and OKAY keeps them. Otherwise they are dropped (drop_pending_memorize) and the spells the member knows listed (list_known_spells): none gives IS NOT A SPELLCASTER! (message 35). Shows SPELLS LEFT TO MEMORIZE (show_spells_left) and the list under MEMORIZE and 'S BOOK OF (spell_screen); afterwards the memorized spells are sorted (sort_memorized) and the choice confirmed, and CANCEL drops it.
list_memorizing, then confirm_chosen.
With spells on the list ($29BD): shows them under 'S CHOSEN (message 59) and asks ARE YOU SURE ABOUT YOUR CHOICE OF SPELLS? (40), carry clear for OKAY. With none, carry set.
The spells being memorized (bit 7 of the memorized bytes $6B20-$6B70), without the bit, into the spell list at $9700.

Adds the spell picked to the first empty memorized byte ($6B20 on) with bit 7 set, being memorized. When that takes the member over its spells for the level (count_spells_left negative) it is taken back by loading the character again, with CAN'T MEMORIZE (message 9). Otherwise its level adds to the levels to memorize ($28A3) and the hours of rest before studying ($28B3) go up to the level's (rest_hours_by_level); WILL MEMORIZE (message 54) and the spell's name, then SPELLS LEFT TO MEMORIZE. Returns the number of classes and levels with spells left, or $FF.

SPELLS LEFT TO MEMORIZE: (message 36) and, for each spell level the member has spells at ($6BED + level), the number left for each class, cleric then magic-user with a slash between, two spaces between levels. With none left at all, CAN'T MEMORIZE ANY MORE SPELLS (message 8). Returns the total.

For each spell level from 9 down to 1 that the member has spells at: counts the memorized spells of that level, one in the low four bits for a magic-user's and $10 for a cleric's, and puts in spells_left the number left for each class, $F (or $F0) when it is over. Returns $FF when any class at any level is over, otherwise the number of class and level pairs that have spells left.
What one spell adds to the count: 1 for a magic-user's, $10 for a cleric's.
The four bits for each class: $0F the magic-user's, $F0 the cleric's.
The VIEW screen's SPELLS while the camp runs: the spells memorized (list_memorized) under 'S MEMORIZED, to look at only.
The spell screen's menu: the count (6), no heading, CAST, MEMORIZE, SCRIBE, NEXT, PREV and EXIT; the mask $2884 shows one of the first three, and NEXT and PREV as the pages allow.
Message 11, "CAST".
Message 12, "MEMORIZE".
Message 13, "SCRIBE".
The hours of rest needed before spells of each level can be studied: 4 for levels 1 and 2, 6 for 3 and 4.
spell_screen_with the heading by the mode in A: 'S MEMORIZED for casting, 'S BOOK OF for memorizing, 'S SCROLL for scribing (messages 56 to 58).

The spell screen: the mode A in $2884 (its low three bits CAST, MEMORIZE or SCRIBE, none to look only, and the bits of the other items), the title CAST, MEMORIZE or SCRIBE (messages 11 to 13) and the heading X (message 56 to 59). Shows the list's first page under the member's name and heading, then the menu: NEXT and PREV turn the pages; CAST, MEMORIZE or SCRIBE picks a spell from the page, with EXIT under it, and does that with it. EXIT clears $29BF and returns.
The page from its start: NEXT is left out when the page shows the end of the list.
The spell screen's menu, the cursor at the start.
PREV: back a page; NEXT is offered again, and PREV no more at the list's start.
NEXT: on a page; PREV is offered, and NEXT no more at the list's end.

A spell from the page: the page's menu comes back (restore_spell_menu) with EXIT under it at column 2, PICK A SPELL TO (message 14) and the title on the bottom row. EXIT or the left arrow goes back to the bar. The spell is done by the mode's low bits: cast (cast_from_list, unless from a scroll, where USE casts it), memorized (memorize_spell) or scribed (scribe_spell).
Casting: from a scroll ('S SCROLL, message 58) the choice is returned for USE; otherwise it is cast, the memorized list made again, and the page drawn again, one back if the page is now past the end.
The spell screen's heading at the top: the member's name, the heading ($2883) and SPELLS (message 55).
The CONFIRM menu: the count (2), CONFIRM:, OKAY and CANCEL.
ARE YOU SURE ABOUT (message 39) and message X on the next row, typed, then CONFIRM: OKAY CANCEL until one is chosen: carry clear for OKAY, set for CANCEL.
The REST menu: the count (4), no heading, REST, INCREASE, DECREASE and EXIT.
The five-minute steps the rest time starts with: 3 for each level of spells to study, 12 for each hour of rest needed first.

REST: the rest time starts at 0 days, 0 hours, 0 minutes. Every member with spells to memorize or scribe counts in $28C5, and the rest time is set to fit the most: 15 minutes for each level of spells, and the most hours of rest needed first. Then REST TIME = DAYS HRS MINS (message 0) and the menu: INCREASE and DECREASE change it by five minutes a press, faster after every ten presses in a row (two more steps a press, $28E0); REST starts it; EXIT leaves.
Five minutes off the rest time, borrowing from the hours and the days; it stops at 0.
Five minutes onto the rest time, carrying into hours and days; at 100 days it takes them off again.
Prints the rest time's days, hours and minutes (rest_time_columns, a space before each under 10) on the row under the top of the window.
The columns of the minutes, hours and days in REST TIME = DAYS HRS MINS: 28, 21 and 13.

REST: with spells to study the spells' names are loaded. The counters start: every third pass of five minutes a quarter hour, every twelfth an hour; no member is ready to study, and the timed effects are aged.

Each pass: five minutes off the rest time and onto the clock (pass_minutes), and the rest time shown. Every quarter hour each member who is studying and ready counts down its spell ($28AB), and when the spell is done it is finished (finish_study) and the next started (next_study). Every hour each member still resting before studying counts its hours down ($28B3), and at 0 is ready ($28BD = $FF) and starts its first spell. Every 24 hours of rest everyone heals (daily_heal).

The rest can be interrupted, in an area that sets $6DD2: every $6DD2 passes a roll of 0 to 99 (roll_die's 1 to 100 less one) under $6DD3, the chance in 100, ends it: $6DD3 = $FF, the studies cancelled and YOUR REST IS RUDELY INTERRUPTED!
The rest ends when the time is used up or the space bar is pressed; whatever is not finished is cancelled (cancel_studies).
With nobody studying ($28C5 = 0) and no timed effect with time left, sets $28C6 so that pass_minutes stops looking at them.

For member $6DB4: the next spell to study (next_study_spell); none left ends its studies (one fewer studying, drop_pending_memorize). Otherwise its countdown ($28AB) is the spell's level in quarter hours: 15 minutes for each level.

For member $6DB4, the spell just studied. One being memorized (bit 7) is memorized: the bit is cleared and HAS MEMORIZED (message 26) printed. One being scribed goes into the spell book ($6B78, its bit), is taken off the scroll ($6D89 and on) and out of the member's scribe list (the last clears it, drop_scribe_list), and the scroll uses up a spell (use_scroll_word): HAS SCRIBED (message 22). Then the member is stored and the screen redrawn.
The second word of the scroll's name ($6D7E) goes down by one, from the word for three spells to two to one; below $D2 the scroll is gone ($6D7C = 0).
Clears every memorized byte still being memorized (bit 7) and the member's levels to memorize ($28A3); with nothing to scribe either, its hours of rest needed ($28B3) too.
Empties the member's scribe list ($6C01, $6C02) and its levels to scribe ($289B), then the same check on the hours needed.
With nothing left to study the hours of rest needed are cleared; the member is stored.
For all eight members: drops what is being memorized and scribed and sorts the memorized spells; the scribe list starts again at its beginning ($2894 = 0).
The member's next scribe list entry (from $6C01, $6C02 of them), passing over the crossed-out ones: loads its scroll and returns the spell (scribe_entry_spell); 0 with none.
For a scribe list entry A: loads the item in its low four bits and returns the spell, of the three at $6D89, that its high four bits pick, X its number.
The member's next spell to study: a scroll's spell first (next_scribe_entry); otherwise the first byte being memorized (bit 7 set, Y its place), or 0 with Y = 0.
Loads the character, copies its memorized bytes ($6B20-$6B70) to $28E8 and puts them back sorted by spell number, from spell 55 down, those being memorized among them; stores it.

After each 24 hours of rest: each member gets one hit point (SPELLE04's heal_member, $A88C, with $2875 = 1), then the party list and THE WHOLE PARTY IS HEALED! (messages 31 and 32), and the rest screen again.
The lower text window from two rows down, cleared, with the text typed.
The rest screen again: REST TIME and the time.

Asks for an amount of coin kind $6D65 ($6D66 twice that, the offset in the money): message $6D62 (TRADE HOW MUCH or DROP HOW MUCH) on the bottom row, the coin's name after it, then the amount, starting at 0. Digits type it in, up to five; INST/DEL starts again at 0; RETURN or the fire button take it; the left arrow makes it 0 and takes it. The joystick right adds one and left takes one away, going round between 0 and the most allowed (amount_max).
The coins' names among LIBRARY's messages, by kind: 34 to 39 COPPER to GEMS, 57 JEWELRY.
The amount ($6D75/$6D76) to 0.
The amount to Y (low) and A (high).
The amount in A (low) and X (high).
One less; below 0 it goes to the most allowed.
One more; past what is allowed it goes back to 0.
amount_zero.
The digit typed: the first replaces the 0; up to the fifth, the amount times ten plus the digit (multiply_16x8); one that would go over what is allowed makes it the most allowed.
For the member taking coins: its figures worked out, and the weight it can still carry, the most (max_load) less what it carries ($6DF6/$6DF7), into $6D63/$6D64, 0 when it carries too much already.
The most allowed: the smaller of the giver's coins of that kind ($6D67 + $6D66) and the spare weight ($6D63/$6D64).
Carry clear when the amount is no more than the coins there are and no more than the spare weight.
A short wait after a joystick step.

SELECT TYPE OF COIN (message 3) on the bottom row, and the money listed on the character screen made a menu at column 12 (list_menu, from the row after $48F0), with EXIT after it. Returns the kind chosen ($6D59) in A and $6D65, or $FF for EXIT.
Copies the working character's money ($6BBB, fourteen bytes) to $6D67.
Copies it back from $6D67.

The VIEW screen's DROP while the camp runs: drops coins. DROP HOW MUCH (message 16): the character screen, a kind of coin (choose_coin) and an amount up to all of them (amount_editor), which is taken from the character's money; again until EXIT.
The amount taken from the kept money of the kind ($6D67 + $6D66).

The VIEW screen's TRADE while the camp runs: gives coins. TRADE TO? (trade_to) picks the member; then TRADE HOW MUCH (message 15), the giver's character screen and a kind of coin (choose_coin, EXIT goes back to TRADE TO). The amount is limited by the giver's coins and what the taker can still carry (spare_capacity); it is added to the taker's money and taken from the giver's, both stored, and the giver is shown again.
Multiplies A (low) and X (high) by Y: the 16-bit product in $4C/$4D and in A and X.

HALVE: splits a stack ($6D86, the count): CAN'T HALVE THAT (message 2) for a single item. The item keeps the larger half and the other half, not readied, goes in the lowest empty slot ($6DE9); a count of 1 stays as it is.

JOIN: every other item carried that is the same as the item in hand, all but its flags ($6D82) and count ($6D86), is added to its count and emptied (join_stack). The item in hand is kept at $6D45 meanwhile (keep_item).
Adds the item's count to the kept item's, unless that would reach 251 or more, and empties the item.

Messages 11 to 13 are the spell menu's own CAST, MEMORIZE and SCRIBE.

The camp messages' addresses, low bytes, by number (72 of them); the high bytes are at $2819.
The camp messages' addresses, high bytes.
$FF while a menu lets up and down move the party cursor; run_menu clears it once a choice is made.
The column the amount is printed at, after the coin's name.
The disk side in the drive before SAVE or ICON asked for another, asked for again afterwards.
The message being typed (type_message, bottom_message and the others).
The minutes pass_minutes adds, for ageing the effects counted in minutes.
The scribe list entry check_scribing found for the item.
Three bytes nothing uses, to $2869.
The cursor run_menu starts on, and leaves on the choice.
The ENCAMP menu's last choice.
The ALTER menu's last choice.
The MAGIC menu's last choice.
A byte nothing uses, after the MAGIC menu's cursor.
The spell print_name_spell prints, or the question check_scribing asks.
The member casting, or DISPLAY's choice ($FF for the whole party).
The timed effect's time left, while age_effect works on it; the bytes to $2877 are work bytes of SPELLE04's.
The hit points heal_member gives (1 after a day's rest).
The level the spell is cast at: the caster's class level, or 6 from a scroll.
A byte SPELLE04's routines use; nothing in the camp uses the one after it.
Cleared before a spell is cast; SPELLE04's routines count into it.
The effect kind DISPLAY is looking for, 1 to 63.
DISPLAY's rows left on the page; SPELLS LEFT TO MEMORIZE's first-item flag; count_spells_left's count.
run_menu's idle count, the inner one.
The idle count's outer one.
4 while the camp picture is on show, so that run_menu animates it; 0 while the screen is used for something else.
A byte nothing uses, after picture_on.
The spell screen's title, message 11, 12 or 13 (CAST, MEMORIZE, SCRIBE).
The spell screen's heading, message 56 to 59 ('S MEMORIZED, 'S BOOK OF, 'S SCROLL, 'S CHOSEN).
The spell screen's mode and its menu's mask: bit 0 CAST, 1 MEMORIZE, 2 SCRIBE, 3 NEXT, 4 PREV, 5 EXIT.
Spells left to memorize by level, the magic-user's count in the low four bits and the cleric's in the high (count_spells_left); $2885 itself is the count of the level in hand.
The spell level count_spells_left and show_spells_left are on.
An index those routines borrow.
The item picked from the spell page.
The scribe list entry for the spell picked; list_scroll_spells's count.
check_scribe's message.
Where the next scribe list entry goes; negative when the list is full.
A byte many routines borrow: a spell number, a level's count, sort_memorized's spell number.
The spells memorized, for CAST; also a level's allowance in show_spells_left.
Where sort_memorized puts the next byte.
The rest time: minutes, in fives.
The rest time's hours.
The rest time's days.
For each party slot, the levels of the spells it is to scribe.
For each party slot, the levels of the spells it is to memorize.
For each party slot, the quarter hours left on the spell it is studying.
For each party slot, the hours of rest it needs before it can study.
The most levels any member has to study, for the rest time.
The most hours any member must rest first.
For each party slot, $FF once its hours of rest are done and it is studying.
How many members have spells to study; also show_spells_left's total.
Set when no timed effect is left to age; pass_minutes then leaves them alone.
The spell's seven bytes from the spell table, $28C7-$28CD.
Whom the spell can be cast on outside combat, for SPELLE04's choose_target: bit 0 the caster, bit 1 a member chosen, bit 2 or 7 the whole party; 0 for a spell only for combat.
Bit 7 set for a cleric's spell; the low seven bits the kind of timed effect it makes, by which DISPLAY names the effects.
The spell's routine, low byte, which cast_spell jumps to.
The spell's routine, high byte.
ORDER's new position for each party slot, $FF for one not yet placed.
ORDER's position count: one less than the positions still to give.
A counter the rest's routines borrow.
Passes to the next quarter hour, from 3.
Passes to the next hour, from 12.
Passes to the next hour of the day's count, from 12; started on arrival, so that rests on one visit add up.
Hours to the next day's healing, from 24.
Passes to the next roll for an interruption, from $6DD2.
The save file being written, 1 then 0; also an index check_scribe borrows.
The target the spell was cast on (choose_target), or the member an ending effect was on.
A byte nothing uses, after spell_target.
INCREASE and DECREASE's extra steps; check_scribe's end of the member's entries.
The timed effect pass_minutes is on.
Presses in a row on INCREASE or DECREASE.
Set once the spell has been cast.
Where the spell comes from: 0 memory, 1 a scroll, 2 another item.
The slot of the item a spell was cast from.
The clock figures that came round, one bit each (clock_add).
The value an effect handler is called with: 0 to start an item's effect, $80 to end it, or the value an effect kept.
81 bytes: CAST's spells set aside, the scroll entries of SCRIBE's list, sort_memorized's copy.

The scribe list, 128 entries for the whole party: each the spell's place on its scroll (times 16) and the scroll's item slot, $FF when crossed out; each member's run of them starts at $6C01, $6C02 long.
The first spell on the page shown.
The spell after the last on the page.
The spell being put on the page.
list_known_spells's spell number.
How many spells are on the list at $9700.
The spell level of the last heading printed.
The spell chosen, to cast, memorize or scribe; 0 after EXIT.

The spells in the member's book: rotates the 33 bytes from $6B78 through the carry 256 times, each bit coming out as spell 0 to 255 in turn, and lists each one set at $9700. The bytes are left turned round; the character is loaded again before they are used.
The spells memorized, not those being memorized (bit 7), from the last byte to the first, at $9700.
show_page from the list's start.
Measures the page from spell A (measure_page), then shows it (show_page_items).

Prints the page's spells from row 3, each a menu item (its number the key, at column 3, 32 wide) with its name two columns in, and before the first of each level the level's heading in white. Then keeps the menu (keep_spell_menu) and makes it a vertical one.
From spell A: how many fit on the page, one row each and two more before each new level, up to row 21 (a heading only before row 18); $29BA the spell after the last.
Y = spell X of the list, A its level; Z clear when it is not the level of the last heading ($29BE, set to it).
Row 3, and no heading printed yet; falls into the RTS at $2AB8.

An RTS, page_top's, that is also the first byte of the level headings' address table: low bytes by level here, $2AB9 for level 1 to $2ABC for level 4, and high bytes from $2ABC, so that level 4's low byte and level 0's high byte are the same byte.
Level 1's heading address, low byte, then levels 2 to 4.
The headings' addresses, high bytes, by level from 0.
The headings: 1ST LEVEL, 2ND LEVEL, 3RD LEVEL, and for level 4, 7TH LEVEL.
The page from the spell after this one's last.
The page before: steps the start back one spell at a time until a page from there ends where this one starts, or the list's start.
Copies the menu's count ($6E93) and its tables (80 bytes from $6E96) to $9780, for pick_spell.
Copies them back, a vertical menu.
The level of spell Y: 1 below 22, 2 below 36, 3 below 56, 4 from 56.

The spells of the scroll in hand. Its name is shown in full (bits 0-2 of $6D82 cleared, and the item and character stored) when the member has a timed effect of kind 16, or has no cleric level, or the scroll is of type $0C. A scroll whose name is shown has its spells, those of $6D89-$6D8B that are not 0, listed at $9700; one still hidden lists none.
The branch's offset; DUNGEON2's code at $7A4C refers to $2B4F, a variable of the adventure module's when that module is in.
The spell onto the list at $9700.
The list's address, the operand of the STA; DUNGEON2's code at $7A56 refers to $2B75, the adventure module's party_map_x when that module is in.
